children: Indian rice export prices were steady this week near their highest level in more than a year, as elevated prices curbed demand, while Vietnamese and Thai rates declined.
India's 5% broken parboiled variety (RI-INBKN5-P1) was quoted at $375-$381 per metric ton, unchanged from last week. Indian 5% broken white rice was priced at $375-$380 per ton.
"The price rise is prompting buyers to pause purchases. They are waiting for prices to come down," said a Kolkata-based trader.

The country's rice production is set to fall this year for the first time in a decade, and by the most in nearly 20 years, as below-normal rainfall during the crop's maturation period threatens to cut yields, industry officials told Reuters.
In Thailand, 5% broken rice prices (RI-THBKN5-P1) dropped to $460 per ton from $470 last week.

Easing concerns over El Niño have prompted millers to release stocks, a Bangkok-based trader said. On the demand side, there have not been any orders for large volumes, and some buyers are still awaiting deliveries of earlier purchases, the trader added.
Meanwhile, Vietnam's 5% broken rice (RI-VNBKN5-P1) was offered at $430 per metric ton on Thursday, down from $440-$445 a week ago.
"Demand remains weak, and trading activity is slow," a trader in Ho Chi Minh City said.

Vietnam exported 189,206 tons of rice in the first half of September, bringing the country's total rice shipments this year through September 15 to 6.12 million tons, valued at $2.93 billion, according to the government's customs data.

Rice prices in Bangladesh have remained elevated, while this week's fuel price increase of up to 17.4% could further stoke inflation in the country by increasing transportation and agricultural production costs, adding to the financial burden on consumers.
